notes:
Inbound SMB (self-serve) signup converted to lead after trial usage. Early discovery focused on security documentation and commercial sizing.

Background:
- Small ecommerce platform (headless storefront + customer support). Mostly US customers; moderate PII (customer emails, order ids).
- Trialers used hosted API for support-agent prototypes and FAQ embeddings. Liked latency and token pricing.

Security ask / props:
- Asked for SOC2 Type II report ("we need to show this to procurement") — requested by their procurement/legal.
- Needs DPA with standard EU/US clauses; wants to review redlines.
- Requested full sub-processor list + short description of purpose (metrics, payments, monitoring).
- Verbal: "We cannot ship any user PII to unknown processors — need clarity on dataflow and retention."

Requirements & constraints:
- Deployment: hosted API on public cloud acceptable. No VPC/private deploy planned for now.
- Throughput/latency: chat responses target ~300-500ms p95 for user-facing helper. Low concurrency initially (hundreds of requests/day).
- Cost sensitivity: medium-high — SMB budget, will watch per-token costs and want clear burst pricing.
- Model preferences: open to Redwood curated open models + fallback to smaller variants for cheap paths. No fine-tuning needed initially.
- Routing/availability: want US regional routing, fallback to multi-region if outage.

Timeline & activities:
- 2026-03-01: Self-serve signup + initial API calls (trial credit).
- 2026-03-05: Intro call (30m) — demo of hosted API usage, quick POC review. Fireflies id attached.
- 2026-03-08: SE follow-up — sent sample integration notes and cost estimate.
- 2026-03-10: Legal requested SOC2 and DPA; Maya requested sub-processor CSV from Redwood.

Quotes / signals:
- "We like the dev experience and the streaming SDK — want to move quickly but legal is cautious."
- Interested in Redwood's Optimize suggestions for batching to reduce spend.

Next steps (short):
